evidence: Col. 5.2.1: multiplicantur in sē duo latera (Lewis & Short)
Col. 5.2.3: lātitūdinis pedēs cum longitūdinis pedibus sīc multiplicābis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Columella’s word for the surveyor’s sums: one number is multiplied cum another, or two in sē, together. Classically also to increase many times over (see increase). Multiplication is multiplicātiō (Col. 5.2.1, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Quattuor cum tribus multiplicā: quot fīunt? — Duodecim.
phrases.english: Multiply four by three: what does it make? — Twelve.

sources: Lewis & Short: multiplico · Lewis & Short: multiplicatio
